LICENCE NOT CONFIRMED: standardwebhooks 1.1.1

The npm package standardwebhooks 1.1.1 declares "license": "MIT" in its package.json.
It is a runtime dependency of the Anthropic SDK (@anthropic-ai/sdk), so it ships with Plenum.
The npm package does not ship a licence file, so its licence text cannot be copied from the package.
The upstream repository (https://github.com/standard-webhooks/standard-webhooks) was checked again in October 2026, from the files themselves and not from a summary:
- Its root LICENSE file is the Apache License, Version 2.0 (11357 bytes, which is the size of the standard Apache-2.0 text). GitHub lists the repository's licence as Apache-2.0.
- libraries/javascript/package.json in that repository declares "license": "MIT", the same as the npm package, and the library folder has no licence file of its own.
The repository's licence file and the package's declaration therefore disagree, and this check does not settle which one applies to the JavaScript library.

Before a release: the developer decides which licence applies (MIT and Apache-2.0 are both on the allowlist), replaces this file with the full licence text and copyright line, and then sets this entry's status to confirmed in scripts/third-party-notices.mjs.
While this entry is unconfirmed, scripts/third-party-notices.mjs prints a warning and marks the entry in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt. With PLENUM_RELEASE=1 the build fails until it is confirmed.
